jsonld.headline: A regular zero-area singularity with a nonzero weak Bianchi defect
jsonld.description: A classical negative-mass geometry has regular zero-area singularities on static slices but a nonzero weak Bianchi boundary functional under retained-sphere vector tests.
jsonld.abstract: We apply a negative-mass member of the known Dadhich–Kar–Mukherjee–Visser metric family to the regular-zero-area-singularity conjecture in Burtscher's Oberwolfach report. Its natural static slices have harmonically regular zero-area singularities of mass −2a, but the homogeneous weak second Bianchi identity fails under the boundary-reaching vector-test convention of Burtscher–Kiessling–Tahvildar-Zadeh. We prove absolute convergence of the full scalar contraction for every such compactly supported smooth test and compute its exact boundary functional; a normalized radial test gives −8π. The metric and its Einstein tensor are classical, and the flux method is already present in the cited weak-identity work. The contribution is this explicit counterexample application and its convergence check. The example violates the null energy condition. The conclusion concerns the geometric implication in the cited static-foliation framework, with no specified matter model; it asserts neither regularity on every arbitrary tilted slice nor an identity for tests smooth after collapsing the boundary sphere to a point.
